title: Sign Safety of Customer-Randomized Experiments in Marketplaces with Heterogeneous Listings under Multinomial Logit Demand
banked_reason: D0.5.G tier=subfield < floor=field (target=field) and NOT salvageable in scope
gap_reasons: The exact necessity frontier stops at J=2 and C=1; for arbitrary markets the protected multiplier condition is only sufficient, with no characterization of the unsafe complement.

The two-type analytic threshold is sharp only on a hand-selected one-dimensional slice, while the broader semialgebraic region is defined partly by the sign polynomial Phi<0 and therefore does not provide an economically interpretable phase diagram.
paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the protected finite-market class, exact two-listing one-type release-rate boundary, customer-heterogeneity reversal, non-A/A null, and a sharp analytic reversal threshold on a parameter slice. The D0.5 math panel passed with no findings, but the novelty gate placed the completed package at subfield against the fixed field floor. A necessary-and-sufficient release-vector characterization for arbitrary finite J remains a separate research program; two decision-panel positioning edits also remain open.
tldr: Customer randomization is sign-safe for rollout bookings only under explicit structure once inventory is heterogeneous. For two equal-release listings with the displayed specialist--flexible two-type primitive MNL family, rollout reverses sign exactly when \(\tau>\rho_+\), where \(558<\rho_+<559\), while the experimental contrast is positive on the maximal admissible design interval \(a\in(0,1)\). The arbitrary-market protected multiplier class yields \(0<\mathsf{GTE}\leq\mathsf{ADE}_a\) and strict A/A null reduction; the one-type two-listing boundary is exactly equality of release rates, whereas unequal releases or customer heterogeneity permit strict sign reversals.
gap: The homogeneous-listing decision theorem relies on a scalar birth--death order and explicitly stops at heterogeneous listings; the finite heterogeneous MNL model has listing-specific releases but its analytic bias theory is mean-field and extreme-market rather than a finite stationary sign classification.
fill: The project combines an arbitrary-market protected multiplier class, a necessary-and-sufficient two-listing release-rate boundary, robust equal-release customer-type failure, and a primitive non-A/A null, all in the published finite MNL inventory model.
